# Gilbert Blythe

- **Age:** nearly fourteen in Volume 1  <sub>[v1 c15 P24](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0024)</sub>
- **Gender:** male  <sub>[v1 c15 P28](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0028)</sub>

## Appearance

Gilbert is a tall, handsome boy with curly brown hair, roguish hazel eyes, and a broad-shouldered, frank-faced appearance. As a youth, he had a mouth twisted into a teasing smile and clear, straightforward eyes. When recovering from severe illness, he appeared noticeably pale and thin.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P16](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0016), [v1 c15 P28](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0028), [v2 c19 P50](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0050), [v3 c39 P22](../source/v03-c39.md#nw-v03-c39-p0022)_

## Personality

Gilbert is good-natured, determined, and full of ambition and zest for life. He possesses a strong sense of humor, an aptitude for teasing, and a deep spirit of self-sacrifice. Clever, hard-working, and academically successful, he approaches both his work and personal ambitions with thoughtful earnestness.

_Sources: [v1 c17 P36](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0036), [v1 c35 P3](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0003), [v1 c38 P38](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0038), [v2 c7 P14](../source/v02-c07.md#nw-v02-c07-p0014), [v3 c25 P25](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0025), [v3 c27 P36](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0036)_

## History

Gilbert Blythe spent three years in Alberta with his father before returning to Avonlea, where he attended school and engaged in a prolonged academic rivalry with Anne Shirley. After attending Queen's Academy and completing Second Year work in one year, he taught school at White Sands to earn money for college, relinquishing the Avonlea school to Anne so she could remain near Green Gables. During his teaching years, he served as president of the Avonlea Village Improvement Society. Gilbert later attended Redmond College, where he led the Freshmen to victory in the Arts Rush, was elected class president, captained the Freshman football team, and ultimately graduated with High Honors in Classics and the Cooper Prize. Following a life-threatening bout of typhoid fever, he confessed his lifelong love for Anne, and they eventually married. Gilbert completed his medical training and took over the practice of his great-uncle, Dr. David Blythe, in Four Winds, before relocating his family to Ingleside in Glen St. Mary.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P24](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0024), [v1 c17 P36](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0036), [v1 c34 P11](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0011), [v1 c36 P24](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0024), [v1 c38 P38](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0038), [v2 c6 P8](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0008), [v3 c5 P0](../source/v03-c05.md#nw-v03-c05-p0000), [v3 c6 P6](../source/v03-c06.md#nw-v03-c06-p0006), [v3 c39 P23](../source/v03-c39.md#nw-v03-c39-p0023), [v3 c40 P9](../source/v03-c40.md#nw-v03-c40-p0009), [v3 c41 P29](../source/v03-c41.md#nw-v03-c41-p0029), [v4 c1 P18](../source/v04-c01.md#nw-v04-c01-p0018), [v4 c4 P15](../source/v04-c04.md#nw-v04-c04-p0015), [v4 c4 P17](../source/v04-c04.md#nw-v04-c04-p0017), [v4 c40 P17](../source/v04-c40.md#nw-v04-c40-p0017), [v5 c30 P14](../source/v05-c30.md#nw-v05-c30-p0014)_

## Quotes

> Corporal punishment as a last resort is to be my rule.  <sub>[v2 c4 P12](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0012)</sub>

> It’s a splendid profession. A fellow has to fight something all through life . . . didn’t somebody once define man as a fighting animal? . . . and I want to fight disease and pain and ignorance . . . which are all members one of another. I want to do my share of honest, real work in the world, Anne . . . add a little to the sum of human knowledge that all the good men have been accumulating since it began. The folks who lived before me have done so much for me that I want to show my gratitude by doing something for the folks who will live after me. It seems to me that is the only way a fellow can get square with his obligations to the race.  <sub>[v2 c7 P14](../source/v02-c07.md#nw-v02-c07-p0014)</sub>

> I must. Things can’t go on like this any longer. Anne, I love you. You know I do. I—I can’t tell you how much. Will you promise me that some day you’ll be my wife?  <sub>[v3 c20 P31](../source/v03-c20.md#nw-v03-c20-p0031)</sub>

> There was nobody else—there never could be anybody else for me but you. I’ve loved you ever since that day you broke your slate over my head in school.  <sub>[v3 c41 P29](../source/v03-c41.md#nw-v03-c41-p0029)</sub>

> You must take your doctor’s advice. There’s an old proverb to the effect that shoemakers’ wives go barefoot and doctors’ wives die young. I don’t mean that it shall be true in my household. You will keep Susan until the old spring comes back into your step, and those little hollows on your cheeks fill out.  <sub>[v4 c22 P2](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0002)</sub>
